content.value_statement: Messy invoice folders slow tax preparation and expense review. This skill extracts key details, renames files, organizes folders, and creates accounting summaries.
actual_capabilities: Identifies PDFs, images, screenshots, and email attachments that likely contain invoices or receipts.
Extracts dates, vendors, invoice numbers, amounts, descriptions, and payment clues when visible.
Builds consistent filenames using date, vendor, document type, and short description.
Organizes copies into folders by vendor, category, date period, or tax category.
Creates a CSV-style summary for accountants, reimbursement, or expense tracking.
limitations: It depends on readable document text or visible image content.
It may flag unclear documents for manual review.
It does not replace professional tax or accounting advice.
It needs user approval before moving, copying, or scripting file changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare Freelancer Taxes
use_cases.description: Turn mixed receipts and vendor invoices into tax-year folders with consistent names and a review summary.

use_cases.title: Close Monthly Expenses
use_cases.description: Group last month's receipts by expense category and prepare totals for bookkeeping review.

use_cases.title: Package Records for an Accountant
use_cases.description: Create clean folders, preserve originals, and produce a summary table for accountant handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Folder Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Organize the invoices in this folder. Keep originals, copy organized files into a new Invoices folder, and show the plan before changes.

prompt_templates.title: Vendor and Category Filing
prompt_templates.prompt: Read these receipts, extract date, vendor, amount, and description, then organize copies by year, category, and vendor.

prompt_templates.title: Accountant Summary
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare these invoice files for my accountant. Rename them consistently, flag unclear records, and create a summary with amounts and categories.

prompt_templates.title: Ongoing Workflow Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an ongoing invoice workflow for my Downloads folder. Include a dry run, approval steps, duplicate handling, and a summary report.

output_examples.input: A folder with mixed PDF invoices and receipt images.
output_examples.output: Files are copied into year and category folders. Each filename includes date, vendor, type, and description. A review list marks missing details.
The skill groups receipts by expense category, totals amounts when readable, and prepares a summary for finance review.

output_examples.input: Several files named invoice.pdf from email downloads.
output_examples.output: The skill reads each file, resolves vendor and date details, renames duplicates clearly, and stores originals separately.

best_practices: Start with a copy of the source folder when records are important.
Review the proposed organization plan before approving file changes.
Check the summary file and any Needs Review folder before sharing with an accountant.
anti_patterns: Do not run bulk moves without a preview and user approval.
Do not assume tax categories are final without professional review.
Do not delete originals after organization unless a backup exists.

faq.question: Can it read scanned receipts?
faq.answer: Yes, when visible text is clear enough to read. Unclear receipts should be flagged for review.

faq.question: Does it move files automatically?
faq.answer: It should present a plan first. The skill recommends copying originals unless the user chooses moving.

faq.question: Can it create a spreadsheet?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create a summary table with date, vendor, amount, category, and file path when available.

faq.question: Does it give tax advice?
faq.answer: No. It organizes records and labels possible categories, but accounting decisions need professional review.

faq.question: What file types are supported?
faq.answer: The skill is designed for PDFs, JPG, PNG, screenshots, email attachments, and similar document files.

faq.question: How are duplicates handled?
faq.answer: It can compare file clues and hashes, keep the best copy, and note duplicates in the summary.
